# The Circuit Method™

Predictable revenue, engineered.

Written decisions. Honest odds. Proof of cause.

Author: Noel Pena. More than twenty years in RevOps and sales leadership. He teaches the method. The site does not describe an employer, a client list, or a set of results.

Core line: The model drafts. The owner decides.

A model, including a statistical model or a language model, is a tool inside the method. It may list signals and shape a draft. It does not write the policy, it does not own the odds you will defend on a forecast call, and it does not approve work that reaches a customer or moves money.

## Business motions the method covers

- Pipeline reviews
- Forecast calls
- Lead routing
- Approvals before a customer is contacted or money moves
- Attribution after the result

## Five stages

Signal: what comes in. Name the evidence that is allowed to change a route or a forecast.

Switch: the decision, written with Decision Model and Notation (DMN). Each row can carry a probability. The owner closes the switch.

Current: drafts of the work. A note, a task, a forecast edit, a routing tag. Fluent is not the same as released.

Breaker: a person, a receipt. The receipt names the rule, the odds at the time, who approved, and what was released.

Ground: the outcome returns. Score the forecast across many calls. Ask what caused the result, not only which touch was nearby.

## Glossary

Closed circuit: a full loop.
Open circuit: built, not proved.
Short circuit: skipping a gate.
Owner load: minutes a day the system takes from the owner. No count is published here.

## Forecasting

State a prior you can explain. Let named signals update it. Say the posterior out loud. Later, compare stated odds with how often those calls happened. The honest picture is a diagonal. This site plots no results.

## Causal proof

Credit divides closed work among touches that were present. Cause needs a baseline, named confounders, uncertainty, and a refusal when the case is not shown. Pending is a complete answer in the review.
